scheme_name: Mechanism for Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP)
overview: The Mechanism for Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) through Minimum Support Price (MSP) & Development of Value Chain for MFP is a central sector scheme launched by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, to ensure fair and remunerative prices for tribal MFP gatherers by institutionalizing the value chain through training, sustainable collection, procurement, value addition, infrastructure, and marketing. Implemented by TRIFED as the nodal agency, the scheme aims to empower tribal communities by enhancing their income and livelihoods through sustainable harvesting, skill upgradation, and market linkages, with a focus on women's financial empowerment and convergence with other development partners.
objectives: Provide Minimum Support Price (MSP) to tribal MFP gatherers for forest produces collected by them
Bridge the last mile connectivity between tribals and markets through activation of Haat bazars by strengthening grassroots infrastructure for MFP procurement, storage, transportation, marketing
Provide training and skill upgradation of tribal artisans in a systematic manner by introducing value addition and marketing through tribal groups and clusters
Promote sustainable livelihoods opportunities in tribal areas by creating sustainable value chains of MFP
Strengthen linkage to women's financial empowerment as MFP collection and value addition activity is undertaken by women MFP gatherers
Ensure fair deal to tribals by offering MSP and provisions for value addition
Enhance tribal income and improve quality of life through sustainable and comprehensive implementation of the scheme
Achieve convergence and coherence with other development partners working in the field of tribal development
eligibility: The Scheme covers 50 non-nationalized MFPs (Annexure 1) and includes all states and union territories of India. The scheme is designed to be implemented through State and District level functionaries. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs as the Nodal Ministry will be the Central Apex Committee and responsible for policy, oversight and obtaining and providing budgetary resources for the Scheme. TRIFED will function as the technical support unit for MoTA and will coordinate the implementation and flow of funds of the Scheme through the designated State and other agencies including District Implementing Units through an Executive Committee setup within TRIFED. The Minimum Support Price will be recommended by the Pricing Cell setup in TRIFED. benefits: The Scheme provides direct benefits to the tribal by institutionalizing various avenues in the value chain of MFP such as training, sustainable collection, procurement, value addition, infrastructure, marketing etc. It ensures training on sustainable harvesting with primary level value addition, skill upgradation and processing. The 'Van Dhan Vikas Karyakram' adds to the income and livelihoods for tribals by harnessing the wealth of forests. The programme aims to tap into traditional knowledge & skill sets of tribals to convert the tribal wisdom into a viable economic activity. The Scheme has strong linkage to women’s financial empowerment. MFP collection and value addition activity is also undertaken by women MFP gatherers. The Scheme ensures fair and remunerative price s to the tribals. It provides fair deal to tribals by offering Minimum Support Price to the tribal MFP gatherers for forest produces collected by them. It also pro visions to bridge the last mile connectivity between the tribals and markets through activation of Haat bazars by strengthening of grassroots infrastructure for MFP procurement, storage, transportation, marketing etc. Besides specific thrust is being given under the Scheme on training and skill upgradation of the tribal artisans in a systematic manner by introducing value addition and marketing through tribal groups and clusters.
